memory_update.text: POWL should remain a high-priority direct switchgear/power-distribution candidate, but market cap has moved above the preferred underfollowed small/mid-cap range; future layers should verify whether backlog quality and margin durability still support chokepoint relevance.

NVT added direct switchgear and bus-system exposure through the Avail Electrical Products Group acquisition; this may be underappreciated because the exposure is embedded inside a broader electrical connection and protection company.

ATKR is a weaker but potentially useful adjacent candidate: not a switchgear pure play, but its conduit, fittings, and cable-management products may participate in the same data-center, solar, industrial, and infrastructure power-distribution buildouts.

Layer 2 should explicitly compare direct equipment exposure versus construction/installation exposure; electrical contractors such as MYR Group may be relevant to substation execution but are not equipment bottleneck names.

node: Substation switchgear, busway, and power distribution
summary: Expanded the universe around substation switchgear, busway, and power distribution with a two-lane funnel. Reference context is Hubbell because it has visible utility substation/transmission exposure but is diversified and already institutionally known. The underfollowed lane favors Powell Industries and Atkore as more focused or messier-label beneficiaries, while nVent is included despite larger size because its 2025 Avail Electrical Products Group acquisition added direct switchgear, bus systems, and electrical enclosure exposure tied to utilities and data centers. No buy/sell view is implied.
